This analysis plots DNA content changes across different time points and media conditions for two different Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains (DGY1 / Wildtype and RIM15Δ0). The data were collected using a Cytek flow cytometer. The DNA content is measured using SYTOX Green stain (B2-A channel) while cell size is approximated using the Forward Scatter Area (FSC-A channel).

### Install CytoExplorer package and requirements. Skip if already installed.
```{r include = FALSE}
require("knitr")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(BiocManager)
library(cowplot) 
library(cytolib) 
library(flowCore)
library(flowWorkspace)
library(openCyto)
library(devtools)
library(CytoExploreR)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggridges)
library(grid)
```

```{r}
experiment_details = left_join(exp_details, sample_sheet) %>%
  write_csv("Vignette-Experiment-Details.csv")
```
  
  Add the experiment details metadata to the gating set.  
  **ONLY NEED TO ONCE**

```{r}
for(i in 1:length(names(experiment_details))){
  flowWorkspace::pData(my_gating_set)[names(experiment_details[i])]<-experiment_details[i]
}
```


## STEP 3:  Perform transformation on the gating set
Gate for 1) Cells, 2) Singlets, 3) 1n and 2n DNA content populations
Results in a gating file and gated data. 

**Transform the data**  
Transforming the data makes it easier to interpret visually and well as to draw gates.  
For this vignette's data, when the transformed data are plotted, the zero copy strains take up most of the coordinate plane and the one copy and two copy distributions are very close together. The fluorescence profiles/distributions of the one copy and two copy controls overlap some. They are not mutually exclusive which is a limitation to note. 

This is a useful article if you I want to think about choosing different transformations:
https://dillonhammill.github.io/CytoExploreR/articles/CytoExploreR-Transformations.html

In our case, it was necessary to use a logicle transformation for the `B2-A` values and then
a log transformation for the other values. I could not use `logicle transformation` nor could I use the `log transformation` for all values. 

**IMPORTANT**: If you get an error message*, run the code in the Console, not inside the R notebook. Make sure you reset your working directory in the Console. 

*Error in plot.new() : QuartzBitmap_Output - unable to open file 

```{r}
SYTOX_trans <- cyto_transformer_arcsinh(my_gating_set, channels = c("B2-A"), cofactor = 150) #returns it as a list
FSC_SSC_trans <- cyto_transformer_arcsinh(my_gating_set, channels = c("FSC-A", "FSC-H", "SSC-A", "SSC-H"), cofactor = 500) #log transform the forward and side scatter
combined_trans <- cyto_transformer_combine(SYTOX_trans,FSC_SSC_trans) #combine all transformations
transformed_gating_set <- cyto_transform(my_gating_set, trans = combined_trans) #applies the the transformation and returns it as a gatingSet
```

Check the transformed entire data by plotting B2-A values (SYTOX fluorescence) over FSC-A (cell size approximation).

```{r}
cyto_plot_explore(transformed_gating_set, #plots all FCS files
                  channels_x = "FSC-A",
                  channels_y = "B2-A",
                  axes_limits = "data")
```
**Interpretation:** The cells with similar FSC but low B2-A are the unstained samples we need to gate out later. The cells with higher B2-A values are the SYTOX stained samples which we will use to analyze DNA content changes.

### STEP 4: Control Plotting

We would like to create a page of cowplot compatible plots that show the density distribution of the B2-A and FSC-A values for haploid (DGY1) and diploid (DGY3) strains. In the end, we want to have a 2 x 2 plot grid in this page where the haploid plots are on the first row and the diploids are on the second row. We want the B2-A density distribution plots on the first column and the FSC-A density distribution plots on the second column. It is important to keep in mind that we would like to have the B2-A axis limits to match one another as the haploid and diploid strains will have different DNA amounts and we want to visually compare these two distributions. 

#### Results
```{r}
# Haploid B2-A plot
cyto_plot(transformed_gating_set[97:99,],channels = c("B2-A"), parent = "root", xlim = c(10e3,10e5), title = NA)
p1 <- recordPlot()

# Haploid FSC plot 
cyto_plot(transformed_gating_set[c(7,9,11),],channels = c("FSC-A"), parent = "root", xlim = c(10e3,10e7), title = NA)
p2 <- recordPlot()

# Diploid B2-A plot
cyto_plot(transformed_gating_set[94:96,],channels = c("B2-A"), parent = "root", xlim = c(10e3,10e5), title = NA)
p3 <- recordPlot()

# Diploid FSC plot
cyto_plot(transformed_gating_set[c(4,6,8),],channels = c("FSC-A"), parent = "root", xlim = c(10e3,10e7), title = NA)
p4 <- recordPlot()

# Comnbine the plots into a 2 x 2 grid in cowplot
control_plot_page <- plot_grid(p1, p2, p3, p4, labels = c("A", "B", "C", "D"), ncol = 2, nrow = 2, align = 'v')
ggsave(filename = paste0("control_plot_page_",version_name,".png"), plot = control_plot_page, width = 8, height = 8, dpi = 300)
control_plot_page
rm(control_plot_page) #clean up
rm(p1,p2,p3,p4) #clean up
```

**Interpretation:** The haploid strain has 2 peaks in the B2-A distribution corresponding to 1n and 2n DNA content while the diploid strain has two peaks corresponding to 2n and 4n DNA content. When the X-axes are matched, the data with three replicates exhibited in three separate colors (pink, green and grey), we can clearly see the 2n peaks for haploid (top row) and diploid (bottom row) B2-A plots match. The '% of mode' in these plots is a density representation associated with the CytoExploreR package. Additionally, the FSC-A distributions show that the diploid cells are larger than the haploid cells as expected.

### STEP 6: Plot the DNA Content and Cell Size Distributions for Wildtype (WT) and RIM15Δ0 Strain Samples Grown in Different Media Conditions

We want to plot out all the samples' DNA content and cell size density distributions, and place each strain - media combination into a different page. In each page, we want one replicate's (rep) denstiy distributions in a single column (so 3 columns in each page) while  placing samples from each time point in a different row (so 5 rows in total: 0, 6, 16, 30, and 46 hour time points). In total, we want 12 pages of 15 plots; 6 pages assigned to B2-A density distributions and 6 pages assigned to FSC-A density distributions. In doing so, we want the parent cell population for FSC-A distributions to be the "Unstained" while the parent for the B2-A distribution plots should be "SYTOX+". We want to utilize a similar code strategy as outlined in STEP 4, where we will use the cyto_plot to plot things out, and finally arrange the plots in the format of a page. We need to write a 'for' loop which creates the 15 plot pages one at a time. 

```{r}
# Helper function to extract and plot FSC-A density data
plot_fsc_density <- function(gs, sample_idx, channel = "FSC-A", parent = "Unstained") {
  if (length(sample_idx) == 0) {
    return(ggplot() + theme_void())
  }
  
  cf <- gh_pop_get_data(gs[[sample_idx]], parent, inverse.transform = TRUE)
  ff <- cytoframe_to_flowFrame(cf)
  m <- exprs(ff)
  df <- as.data.frame(m[, channel, drop = FALSE], check.names = FALSE)
  names(df) <- "value"
  
  df_pos <- df[df$value > 0 & is.finite(df$value), , drop = FALSE]
  
  if (nrow(df_pos) == 0) {
    return(ggplot() + theme_void())
  }
  
  ggplot(df_pos, aes(x = value)) +
    geom_density(fill = "steelblue", color = "black", alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 2000000)) +
    labs(x = channel, y = "Density") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5, "pt")
    )
}

# Helper function to create timepoint label
create_timepoint_label <- function(timepoint) {
  ggplot() +
    annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = paste0(timepoint, "h"), 
             size = 5, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5) +
    theme_void()
}

gs_metadata <- pData(transformed_gating_set)

strain_media_combos <- gs_metadata %>%
  dplyr::filter(Sample_type == "Size_control") %>%
  distinct(Strain, Media) %>%
  arrange(Strain, Media)

timepoints <- c(0, 6, 16, 30, 46)

for (i in 1:nrow(strain_media_combos)) {
  strain <- strain_media_combos$Strain[i]
  media <- strain_media_combos$Media[i]
  
  row_plots <- vector("list", length(timepoints))
  
  for (tp_idx in seq_along(timepoints)) {
    timepoint <- timepoints[tp_idx]
    col_plots <- vector("list", 3)
    
    for (rep in 1:3) {
      idx <- which(
        gs_metadata$Strain == strain &
        gs_metadata$Media == media &
        gs_metadata$Time == timepoint &
        gs_metadata$Bio_rep == rep &
        gs_metadata$Sample_type == "Size_control"
      )
      
      col_plots[[rep]] <- plot_fsc_density(transformed_gating_set, idx)
    }
    
    timepoint_label <- create_timepoint_label(timepoint)
    row_with_label <- plot_grid(
      timepoint_label,
      plot_grid(plotlist = col_plots, ncol = 3),
      ncol = 2,
      rel_widths = c(0.08, 0.92)
    )
    
    row_plots[[tp_idx]] <- row_with_label
  }
  
  page_title <- ggdraw() + 
    draw_label(
      paste0(strain, " | Media: ", media, " | FSC-A (Cell Size)"),
      fontface = "bold"
    )
  
  page <- plot_grid(
    page_title,
    plot_grid(plotlist = row_plots, ncol = 1),
    ncol = 1,
    rel_heights = c(0.05, 0.95)
  )
  
  ggsave(
    sprintf("plots/FSC_A_%s_%s.png", strain, media),
    page,
    width = 10,
    height = 12,
    dpi = 300
  )
  print(page)
}

# Helper function to extract and plot B2-A density data
plot_b2a_density <- function(gs, sample_idx, channel = "B2-A", parent = "SYTOX+") {
  if (length(sample_idx) == 0) {
    return(ggplot() + theme_void())
  }
  
  cf <- gh_pop_get_data(gs[[sample_idx]], parent, inverse.transform = TRUE)
  ff <- cytoframe_to_flowFrame(cf)
  m <- exprs(ff)
  df <- as.data.frame(m[, channel, drop = FALSE], check.names = FALSE)
  names(df) <- "value"
  
  df_pos <- df[df$value > 0 & is.finite(df$value), , drop = FALSE]
  
  if (nrow(df_pos) == 0) {
    return(ggplot() + theme_void())
  }
  
  ggplot(df_pos, aes(x = value)) +
    geom_density(fill = "coral", color = "black", alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100000)) +
    labs(x = channel, y = "Density") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5, "pt")
    )
}

# Helper function to create timepoint label
create_timepoint_label <- function(timepoint) {
  ggplot() +
    annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = paste0(timepoint, "h"), 
             size = 5, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5) +
    theme_void()
}

gs_metadata <- pData(transformed_gating_set)

strain_media_combos <- gs_metadata %>%

    for (rep in 1:3) {
      idx <- which(
        gs_metadata$Strain == strain &

        gs_metadata$Time == timepoint &
        gs_metadata$Bio_rep == rep &
        gs_metadata$Sample_type == "DNA_content"

      col_plots[[rep]] <- plot_b2a_density(transformed_gating_set, idx)

    timepoint_label <- create_timepoint_label(timepoint)
    row_with_label <- plot_grid(
      timepoint_label,

```
**Cell Size Data Interpretation:** The cell size distribution seems to be a bimodal distribution, so we need to quantify the median FSC-A values for cell size instead of the mean cell size values. We also need to keep in mind that each sample has been acquired separately, so combining the results of all three samples as if they had the same range of voltages and experimental conditions at the exact instant they were being measured would not be accurate. We therefore need to acquire a median quantification for each sample separately to then quantify the mean of the three median values quantified as our cell size statistic at each time point for each unique media and strain condition. 
**DNA Content Data Interpretation:** The DNA content seems to follow a pattern where the 1n peak increases in size as time goes on while the 2n peak decreases in size. This is expected as cells arrest in G1 phase of the cell cycle under nutrient limitation conditions. We will quantify the percentage of 1n cells in the SYTOX+ parent population to quantify this effect across time and media conditions for both strains.

### STEP 7: Quantify the Percentile Values of DNA Content for All Samples Across Time

Now that we've plotted all the distributions and have observed how they shift, we would like to quantify what percent of SYTOX+ cells have 1n DNA content and how this percentage changes across time. In doing so, we would like to compare, in a 3 plot arrangement, how each media condition (Carbon, Nitrogen or Phosphorus) affects the percentile of 1n DNA content cells for each strain (WT and RIM15Δ0) across time. We will calculate the percentage of 1n cells in the SYTOX+ parent population for all the 3 media conditions having the two strains on the same plot displaying time on the X axis and the 1n percentage on the Y axis. We will then use ggplot to plot out the results. 

```{r}
# Extract cell counts for SYTOX+ and 1n populations
gs_metadata <- pData(transformed_gating_set)

# Get population statistics
results <- data.frame()

for (i in 1:length(transformed_gating_set)) {
  
  # Get metadata for this sample
  strain <- gs_metadata$Strain[i]
  media <- gs_metadata$Media[i]
  timepoint <- gs_metadata$Time[i]
  bio_rep <- gs_metadata$Bio_rep[i]
  sample_type <- gs_metadata$Sample_type[i]
  
  # Only process DNA_content samples
  if (is.na(sample_type) || sample_type != "DNA_content") {
    next
  }
  
  # Include all samples
  if (is.na(media) || is.na(strain)) {
    next
  }
  
  # Get counts for SYTOX+ parent population
  sytox_stats <- gh_pop_get_stats(
    transformed_gating_set[[i]],
    nodes = "SYTOX+"
  )
  sytox_count <- sytox_stats$count[1]
  
  # Get counts for 1n population
  one_n_stats <- gh_pop_get_stats(
    transformed_gating_set[[i]],
    nodes = "1n"
  )
  one_n_count <- one_n_stats$count[1]
  
  # Calculate percentage
  if (sytox_count > 0) {
    pct_1n <- (one_n_count / sytox_count) * 100
  } else {
    pct_1n <- NA
  }
  
  # Add to results data frame
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
    Strain = strain,
    Media = media,
    Time = timepoint,
    Bio_rep = bio_rep,
    Percentage_1n = pct_1n,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ))
}

# Remove rows with NA values
results <- results %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(Strain), !is.na(Media))

# Calculate mean and standard error for each strain-media-timepoint combo
results_summary <- results %>%
  group_by(Strain, Media, Time) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_pct = mean(Percentage_1n, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_pct = sd(Percentage_1n, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Extract T0 Control data
t0_control_data <- results_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(Time == 0, Media == "Control") %>%
  select(Strain, Time, mean_pct, se_pct)

# Convert Time to ordered factor
results_summary$Time <- factor(results_summary$Time, 
                               levels = c(0, 6, 16, 30, 46),
                               ordered = TRUE)

# Rename strains and filter out DGY3
results_summary <- results_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(Strain != "DGY3") %>%
  mutate(Strain = recode(Strain, 
                         "DGY1" = "WT",
                         "RIM15Δ0" = "RIM15\u03940"))

t0_control_data <- t0_control_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(Strain != "DGY3") %>%
  mutate(Strain = recode(Strain, 
                         "DGY1" = "WT",
                         "RIM15Δ0" = "RIM15\u03940"))

# Create plots for each media condition
media_conditions <- c("C", "N", "P")
media_names <- c("Carbon", "Nitrogen", "Phosphorus")

plots <- vector("list", 3)

for (j in seq_along(media_conditions)) {
  media <- media_conditions[j]
  media_name <- media_names[j]
  
  # Get data for this media condition
  data_subset <- results_summary %>%
    dplyr::filter(Media == media)
  
  # Add T0 control data to each plot
  t0_control_plot <- t0_control_data %>%
    mutate(Media = media)  # Assign to current media for plotting
  
  data_combined <- bind_rows(data_subset, t0_control_plot)
  
  # Convert Time to ordered factor
  data_combined$Time <- factor(data_combined$Time, 
                               levels = c(0, 6, 16, 30, 46),
                               ordered = TRUE)
  
  plots[[j]] <- ggplot(data_combined, aes(x = Time, y = mean_pct, 
                                           color = Strain, shape = Strain,
                                           group = Strain)) +
    geom_line(size = 1) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_pct - se_pct, ymax = mean_pct + se_pct),
                  width = 0.2, size = 0.8) +
    labs(title = paste(media_name, "Limitation"),
         x = "Time (hours)",
         y = "Percentage of 1n DNA Content (%)",
         color = "Strain",
         shape = "Strain") +
    ylim(0, 100) +
    theme_cowplot() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.position = "right"
    )
}

# Combine all three plots
combined_plot <- plot_grid(plots[[1]], plots[[2]], plots[[3]], ncol = 3)

# Save the combined plot
ggsave("plots/1n_percentage_across_media.png", 
       combined_plot, 
       width = 16, height = 5)

print(combined_plot)

# Also save the summary data
write_csv(results_summary, "results_1n_percentage.csv")
```
**Interpretation:** The percentage of 1n cells increases over time under all nutrient limitation conditions, indicating that cells are arresting in G1 phase. The WT strain shows a more pronounced increase in 1n percentage compared to the RIM15Δ0 strain, suggesting that RIM15 plays a role in the cell cycle arrest response to nutrient limitation over time.

### STEP 8: Quantify the Median Cell Size Distribution for ALl Samples Across Time

We want to perform the same analysis we have done in STEP 7 but do it on the unstained samples and quantify the median FSC-A values for all samples at different time points in all 3 media conditions. For this analysis, since the FSC-A distributions exhibited a bimodal distribution for some of the samples, we will plot the median FSC-A values for all samples and aim for a better representation of that distribution. 

```{r}
# STEP 8: Quantify the Median Cell Size (FSC-A) for All Samples Across Time
# Combine all replicates for each timepoint and calculate median FSC-A

gs_metadata <- pData(transformed_gating_set)

# Get unique strain-media-timepoint combinations from Size_control samples
unique_combos <- gs_metadata %>%
  dplyr::filter(Sample_type == "Size_control") %>%
  distinct(Strain, Media, Time) %>%
  arrange(Strain, Media, Time)

# Calculate median FSC-A by combining all replicates
results_summary <- data.frame()

for (i in 1:nrow(unique_combos)) {
  strain <- unique_combos$Strain[i]
  media <- unique_combos$Media[i]
  timepoint <- unique_combos$Time[i]
  
  # Get indices for all replicates with this combination
  indices <- which(
    gs_metadata$Strain == strain &
    gs_metadata$Media == media &
    gs_metadata$Time == timepoint &
    gs_metadata$Sample_type == "Size_control"
  )
  
  # Combine FSC-A values from all replicates
  all_fsc_values <- c()
  
  for (idx in indices) {
    cf <- gh_pop_get_data(transformed_gating_set[[idx]], "Unstained", 
                          inverse.transform = TRUE)
    ff <- cytoframe_to_flowFrame(cf)
    m <- exprs(ff)
    fsc_values <- m[, "FSC-A"]
    all_fsc_values <- c(all_fsc_values, fsc_values)
  }
  
  # Calculate median of combined data
  median_fsc <- median(all_fsc_values, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  results_summary <- rbind(results_summary, data.frame(
    Strain = strain,
    Media = media,
    Time = timepoint,
    median_fsc = median_fsc,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ))
}

# Convert Strain to use proper delta symbol
results_summary <- results_summary %>%
  mutate(Strain = recode(Strain, "RIM15Δ0" = "RIM15\u03940"))

# Convert Time to ordered factor
results_summary$Time <- factor(results_summary$Time, 
                               levels = c(0, 6, 16, 30, 46),
                               ordered = TRUE)

# Extract T0 Control data
t0_control_data <- results_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(Time == 0, Media == "Control") %>%
  select(Strain, Time, median_fsc)

# Create plots for each media condition
media_conditions <- c("C", "N", "P")
media_names <- c("Carbon", "Nitrogen", "Phosphorus")

plots <- vector("list", 3)

for (j in seq_along(media_conditions)) {
  media <- media_conditions[j]
  media_name <- media_names[j]
  
  # Get data for this media condition
  data_subset <- results_summary %>%
    dplyr::filter(Media == media)
  
  # Add T0 control data to each plot
  t0_control_plot <- t0_control_data %>%
    mutate(Media = media)
  
  data_combined <- bind_rows(data_subset, t0_control_plot)
  
  # Convert Time to ordered factor
  data_combined$Time <- factor(data_combined$Time, 
                               levels = c(0, 6, 16, 30, 46),
                               ordered = TRUE)
  
  plots[[j]] <- ggplot(data_combined, aes(x = Time, y = median_fsc, 
                                           color = Strain, shape = Strain,
                                           group = Strain)) +
    geom_line(size = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    labs(title = paste(media_name, "Limitation"),
         x = "Time (hours)",
         y = "Median FSC-A",
         color = "Strain",
         shape = "Strain") +
    ylim(300000, 1100000) +
    theme_cowplot() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.position = "right"
    )
}

# Combine all three plots
combined_plot <- plot_grid(plots[[1]], plots[[2]], plots[[3]], ncol = 3)

# Save the combined plot
ggsave("plots/FSC_A_median_across_media.png", 
       combined_plot, 
       width = 16, height = 5)

print(combined_plot)

# Also save the summary data
write_csv(results_summary, "results_FSC_A_median.csv")
```
**Interpretation:** The median FSC-A values decrease over time under all nutrient limitation conditions, indicating that cells are reducing their size in response to nutrient stress. The WT strain shows a more pronounced decrease in cell size compared to the RIM15Δ0 strain, suggesting that RIM15 plays a role in the cell size regulation response to nutrient limitation.

### STEP 9: Creating Panel E for the Paper

In this final step, we synthesize the findings from STEP 7 and STEP 8 into a unified, dual-axis visualization that mimics the format of Panel D in the reference paper. We aim to show the temporal relationship between cell cycle arrest (1n DNA percentage) and morphological changes (Median FSC-A) for both the Wildtype (WT) and RIM15Δ0 strains across the three different media limitation conditions (Carbon, Nitrogen, and Phosphorus).

```{r}
# STEP 9 (MODIFIED): Extract raw FSC-A values instead of sample medians

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(cowplot)

gs_metadata <- pData(transformed_gating_set)

# 1. Modified loop to collect ALL FSC-A values (not just medians)
combined_results <- data.frame()
fsc_values_list  <- list()

for (i in 1:length(transformed_gating_set)) {
  strain      <- gs_metadata$Strain[i]
  media       <- gs_metadata$Media[i]
  timepoint   <- as.numeric(as.character(gs_metadata$Time[i]))
  sample_type <- gs_metadata$Sample_type[i]

  if (is.na(strain) || strain == "DGY3") next

  pct_1n <- NA
  if (!is.na(sample_type) && sample_type == "DNA_content") {
    sytox_stats <- gh_pop_get_stats(transformed_gating_set[[i]], nodes = "SYTOX+")
    one_n_stats <- gh_pop_get_stats(transformed_gating_set[[i]], nodes = "1n")
    if (sytox_stats$count[1] > 0)
      pct_1n <- (one_n_stats$count[1] / sytox_stats$count[1]) * 100
  }

  if (!is.na(sample_type) && sample_type == "Size_control") {
    cf <- gh_pop_get_data(
      transformed_gating_set[[i]], "Unstained",
      inverse.transform = TRUE
    )
    ff <- cytoframe_to_flowFrame(cf)
    m  <- exprs(ff)
    if (nrow(m) > 0) {
      fsc_values_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
        Strain   = strain,
        Media    = media,
        Time     = timepoint,
        SampleID = i,          # biological replicate identifier
        FSC_A    = m[, "FSC-A"]
      )
    }
  }

  combined_results <- rbind(combined_results, data.frame(
    Strain = strain, Media = media, Time = timepoint,
    pct_1n = pct_1n
  ))
}

# 2. Combine all FSC-A values; calculate median per replicate first,
#    then SEM across replicate medians
fsc_data <- bind_rows(fsc_values_list)

t0_size_baseline <- fsc_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(Time == 0, Media %in% c("C", "N", "P")) %>%
  group_by(Strain, Media, SampleID) %>%
  summarise(sample_median = median(FSC_A, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Strain, Media) %>%
  summarise(
    base_size = mean(sample_median, na.rm = TRUE),
    sem_size  = sd(sample_median, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups   = "drop"
  )

time_gt0_size <- fsc_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(Time > 0, Media %in% c("C", "N", "P")) %>%
  group_by(Strain, Media, Time, SampleID) %>%
  summarise(sample_median = median(FSC_A, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Strain, Media, Time) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_size = mean(sample_median, na.rm = TRUE),
    sem_size  = sd(sample_median, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups   = "drop"
  )

# 3. Reconstruct Baselines — SEM across biological replicates for DNA
t0_dna_baseline <- combined_results %>%
  dplyr::filter(Time == 0, Media == "Control") %>%
  group_by(Strain) %>%
  summarise(
    base_dna = mean(pct_1n, na.rm = TRUE),
    sem_dna  = sd(pct_1n, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(pct_1n))),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

master_t0 <- t0_size_baseline %>%
  left_join(t0_dna_baseline, by = "Strain") %>%
  rename(mean_size = base_size, mean_dna = base_dna) %>%
  # sem_size and sem_dna are carried through automatically
  mutate(Time = 0)

# Time > 0 DNA content — SEM across biological replicates
final_df <- combined_results %>%
  dplyr::filter(Media %in% c("C", "N", "P"), Time > 0) %>%
  group_by(Strain, Media, Time) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_dna = mean(pct_1n, na.rm = TRUE),
    sem_dna  = sd(pct_1n, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(pct_1n))),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(time_gt0_size, by = c("Strain", "Media", "Time")) %>%
  bind_rows(master_t0) %>%
  mutate(
    Strain = recode(Strain, "DGY1" = "WT", "RIM15Δ0" = "RIM15\u03940")
  ) %>%
  arrange(Media, Strain, Time)

# 4. Global parameters for dual-axis scaling
raw_min <- min(final_df$mean_size, na.rm = TRUE)
raw_max <- max(final_df$mean_size, na.rm = TRUE)
s_min   <- raw_min * 0.95
s_max   <- raw_max * 1.05
s_range <- s_max - s_min

# Helper: transform FSC-A (or its SEM) to the primary [0,100] axis
to_prim     <- function(x) ((x - s_min) / s_range) * 100
sem_to_prim <- function(s) (s / s_range) * 100

# 5. Plotting Loop
media_types   <- c("C", "N", "P")
media_labs    <- c("Carbon", "Nitrogen", "Phosphorous")
strain_colors <- c("WT" = "#E69F00", "RIM15\u03940" = "#56B4E9")

plots <- list()
for (j in seq_along(media_types)) {
  m_type    <- media_types[j]
  plot_data <- final_df %>% dplyr::filter(Media == m_type)

  plots[[j]] <- ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(x = Time, color = Strain, group = Strain)
  ) +

    # --- DNA Content: solid lines ---
    geom_line(aes(y = mean_dna), linewidth = 1.2, linetype = "solid") +

        # SEM error bars for 1n DNA %
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(
        ymin = mean_dna - sem_dna,
        ymax = mean_dna + sem_dna
      ),
      width     = 1.5,    # <-- increase this
      linewidth = 0.7,
      alpha     = 0.7
    ) +

    # --- Cell Size: dashed lines ---
    geom_line(
      aes(y = to_prim(mean_size)),
      linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed"
    ) +

        # SEM error bars for FSC-A
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(
        y    = to_prim(mean_size),
        ymin = to_prim(mean_size) - sem_to_prim(sem_size),
        ymax = to_prim(mean_size) + sem_to_prim(sem_size)
      ),
      width     = 1.5,    # <-- increase this
      linewidth = 0.7,
      linetype  = "dashed",
      alpha     = 0.7
    ) +

    scale_y_continuous(
      name     = "1n DNA (%) (solid lines)",
      sec.axis = sec_axis(
        ~ . * (s_range / 100) + s_min,
        name   = "Median FSC-A (dashed lines)",
        labels = scales::label_scientific()
      )
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = strain_colors) +
    labs(title = media_labs[j], x = "Time (hours)") +
    theme_cowplot() +
    theme(
      axis.title.y.left  = element_text(color = "blue", size = 10),
      axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "red",  size = 10),
      legend.position    = "none",
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey90", linetype = "dotted")
    )
}

# Combine and Display
legend_d <- get_legend(
  plots[[1]] +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    labs(color = "Genotype", shape = "Genotype")
)

final_panel <- plot_grid(
  plot_grid(plotlist = plots, ncol = 3, align = "h"),
  legend_d,
  ncol        = 1,
  rel_heights = c(1, 0.1)
)

ggsave("plots/Panel_D_DNA_Size.pdf", final_panel,
       width = 16, height = 6, dpi = 300)
print(final_panel)
```

### STEP 10: Replot Individual Plots As Separate Plots

```{r}
# Save DNA (solid) and Size (dashed) as two separate PDF panels
# Assumes you have already run the prior code and have:

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```
